newsitem.title: UK: New British government looks set to ban handguns.
newsitem.headline: New British government looks set to ban handguns.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is set to ban all handguns, carrying out a pledge it made in opposition after a crazed gunman massacred 16 small children and their teacher in a small Scottish school last year.
Aides to Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Tuesday the ban would be included in the new government's legislative programme, to be unveiled by Queen Elizabeth in parliament on Wednesday.

The first people to be told of the ban were a group of the parents whose children were shot dead in March 1996 by loner Thomas Hamilton, who sprayed the gym of the small school in the town of Dunblane with gunfire before killing himself.
Blair met 14 of the parents in the garden of the prime minister's Downing Street office on Tuesday.
A campaign backed by the Dunblane parents gathered 750,000 signatures on a petition calling for a total ban on handguns.

But the ousted Conservative government, faced with protests from shooting organisations, compromised by banning only handguns with a calibre higher than .22, saying the lower calibre guns were used mainly for sporting competitions.
It also promised to pay compensation to gun owners forced to hand in their weapons.
Blair -- swept into power in a landslide election victory 10 days ago -- promised the parents he would now act quickly, if possible making the handgun ban law by the summer.
Labour is committed to giving members of parliament a free vote on the bill, but aides believe there will be overwhelming support for it in the House of Commons where Labour has a majority of 179.
They admit there could be problems in the House of Lords, the upper parliamentary chamber and a bastion of traditional sports. However, there is overwhelming public support for the parents' campaign.

Blair told the parents -- who wound up their personal campaign on election day and put their support behind a London-based anti-handgun pressure group -- he was counting on them to help fight Britain's vocal gun lobby.
